description: Claim 1 is an annual wellness visit with a preventive screening, both covered preventive services. The wellness visit line charges the member the $20 office-visit copay, even though its own note P1 says no copayment, coinsurance or deductible applies. Claim 2, an office visit with lab tests, is correct. A careful reviewer should conclude the member owes $0 for the wellness visit, because Medicare Advantage plans may not charge cost sharing for in-network Medicare-covered preventive services.

sources.what: MA organizations may not charge deductibles, copayments or coinsurance for in-network Medicare-covered preventive services (paragraph (k))
The preventive services this rule covers include the annual wellness visit (paragraph (l))
sources.source: Cornell LII, 42 CFR 410.152 Amounts of payment, https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/42/410.152

sources.what: You pay nothing for the yearly wellness visit if your provider accepts assignment, and the Part B deductible does not apply
